existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `Consent` is the same artifact identity but has substantial local breaking changes. Top concerns are mandatory R4 `scope` removal, required `status` vocabulary changes, policy/provision remodels, and ambiguous actor/policy/content-class migrations. The main uncertainty is lack of official cross-version mappings and narrative rationale.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a domain transform, not a field rename. Several R4 elements were overloaded (`performer`, `policyRule`, `provision.class`) and need local interpretation before mapping. R6 adds more expressive constructs (`subject`, `grantor`/`grantee`, `decision`, `policyBasis`, `provision.expression`) that improve modeling but create lossy R6-to-R4 downgrade paths.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, type, flag, and local terminology deltas because both StructureDefinitions and key local terminology artifacts were inspected. Confidence is medium for the intended migration semantics because official diffs, ballot rationale, full narrative pages, terminology expansions, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not available in the local inputs.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Consent keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 9 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 7 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 1 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 100/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Required Consent.scope was removed and the scope/category model was loosened
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing required `scope` carry an element not allowed by base R6; semantic loss is likely if no explicit category or policy mapping is made.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent.status required code set changed: proposed/rejected removed and not-done/unknown added
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `status` of `proposed` or `rejected` fail R6 required terminology validation; R6 `not-done` and `unknown` are also lossy in R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent.dateTime was replaced by Consent.date, narrowing precision and changing meaning
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `dateTime` is not an R6 element; migration to R6 `date` can truncate time and confuse record/indexing time with agreement date.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent.verification.verificationDate was renamed to date and verification metadata was expanded
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: R4 `verificationDate` is not base R6, and R6 multiple dates or verifier metadata cannot be represented in base R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent.patient was renamed to Consent.subject and reference targets were widened
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON with `patient` is not base R6, generated properties change, and R6 non-Patient subjects cannot be represented in base R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent.provision.class was split into documentType and resourceType with changed bindings
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `provision.class` is not base R6; R6 `documentType` and `resourceType` collapse lossy back into R4's single class bucket.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Consent performer/custodian fields were remodeled into grantor, grantee, manager, and controller
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `performer` and `organization` are not base R6; R6 role-specific actors and widened targets are lossy when downgraded to base R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Policy and policyRule were removed, replaced by regulatoryBasis/policyBasis/policyText, and the R4 policy-or-policyRule invariant disappeared
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `policy` and `policyRule` are not base R6; R6 records with no policy basis also cannot satisfy the old R4 invariant.
